newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mexico chooses Arianespace for satellite launch.
newsitem.headline: Mexico chooses Arianespace for satellite launch.

text.p: Mexico has chosen Arianespace to launch a new telecommunications satellite in late 1998, the Paris-based space firm said on Wednesday.

It said MORELOS III, the fifth satellite of Telecomunicaciones de Mexico, would be launched into space aboard an Ariane rocket from the European Space Agency's Kourou launch centre in equatorial French Guiana.

The satellite, built by Hughes Space and Communications in El Segundo, California, will have a launch weight of 3,550 kg (7,828 lbs) and will be 10 times more powerful than its predecessor MORELOS II, Arianespace said in a statement.
Hughes Space and Communications is a unit of General Motors Corp.
Mexico had previously chosen Arianespace for the launch of its SOLIDARIDAD 1 and 2 satellites in 1993 and 1994.
Arianespace is controlled by French state-owned companies and organisations which hold a 65-percent share in the company. The CNES French space agency owns 32 percent.
